title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 11th Congressional District
area: South-central Pennsylvania: Lancaster County and part of York County.

context.text: Lloyd Smucker was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. Nancy Mannion defeated Sarah Klimm in the Democratic primary. Jeffrey Wilder (Independent) did not make the general-election ballot, according to Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Lloyd Smucker
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2017); member, House Committee on Ways and Means and House Committee on the Budget

priorities.text: Statement on the Working Families Tax Cuts says the Congressional Budget Office confirms the cuts are "accelerating the growth of the American economy."
priorities.quote: When it comes to economic growth, the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has one thing right—the Working Families Tax Cuts (WFTC) are accelerating the growth of the American economy.

priorities.text: Introduced legislation to renew and expand the Work Opportunity Tax Credit, intended to help connect disadvantaged individuals to jobs.

positions.summary: In January 2026 voted against extending the enhanced ACA premium tax credits for three years, saying it would preserve a broken system, and instead backed Republican premium-reduction legislation.
positions.quote: I opposed this short-term extension of COVID-era enhanced tax credits because it preserves a broken system.

record.text: Assigned to the Joint Economic Committee, the Committee on Ways and Means (Social Security, Tax, and Trade subcommittees), and the House Committee on Budget for the 2025-2026 Congress.

Introduced the Improve and Enhance the Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) Act, updated in November 2025, to strengthen and extend a tax credit intended to help disadvantaged individuals secure employment.
Voted for H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act, in May 2023.
Sponsored legislation described by his office as strengthening Social Security and protecting children from identity fraud, passed by the House with near-unanimous support in December 2025.

candidates.name: Nancy Mannion
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary, defeating Sarah Klimm

priorities.text: Says she wants to make life more affordable for district residents, citing farmers struggling with tariffs and fertilizer costs, small businesses facing regulatory burdens, and families struggling to afford groceries and health care.
priorities.quote: Real Care. Real Change. Nancy puts people first: she cares about the issues those in her district care about, whether it's a farmer struggling with tariffs and the high cost of fertilizer, or the small business owner tapped in government red tape.

priorities.text: Cites her nursing career as the basis for evidence-based, pragmatic decision-making, and says she wants to "cool down" partisan political debate.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she will fight to raise the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: She’ll fight to raise the federal minimum wage so folks can afford the basics—like rent and groceries.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she would remove the current tariffs and replace them with targeted ones.
positions.quote: She’d get rid of the tariffs President Trump put in place and swap them for targeted tariffs that protect American jobs.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she supports stronger gun laws.
positions.quote: She supports stronger gun laws and more mental health support in our schools.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says reproductive decisions should be made between the patient, family and a medical provider, without government intrusion.
positions.quote: She believes reproductive decisions should be made only between the patient, their family, and a medical provider. No government should intrude in this decision.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she is not in favor of tax credits or vouchers that send money to private schools.
positions.quote: Nancy is not in favor of tax credits or voucher programs that push money toward private schools.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she would close tax loopholes benefiting wealthy people and big companies and roll back the 2025 corporate tax rate cut.
positions.quote: Nancy’s plan includes rolling back the 2025 corporate tax rate drop.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she supports strong borders and treating immigration violations as civil offenses, with ICE focused on those with serious criminal records.
positions.quote: Immigration violations are a civil offense and should be treated as such. ICE should be focused on those with serious criminal records.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are from the Priorities page of her campaign website (written in the third person) and her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No statements were found on rent regulation, police funding, or Israel. Positions and statements from nancymannion.com/Priorities are third-person campaign text, not her own first-person words. A 'war_powers' statement about unauthorized wars was removed as a budget comment, not a stance on congressional approval.

statements.quote: She’s all for bringing back Affordable Care Act subsidies and expanding childcare tax credits so families can get a break.
statements.context: On her campaign website (third-person campaign text)
